messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas (as of 2024)** | Topic | Key Points | Notes | |-------|------------|-------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits vary by road type (e.g., 55 mph on rural interstates, 45 mph on urban interstates).
• “No‑limit” highways (e.g., I‑10, I‑35) have no posted speed limit, but drivers must drive at a safe speed for conditions. | Speed limits are posted in miles per hour (mph). | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑seat Requirements** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• Children under 4 must be in a rear‑facing seat. | Failure to comply can result in a $50 fine. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | Violations carry a $50 fine and points on the driver’s record. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas has a “zero‑tolerance” law for drivers under 21. | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the driver on the right has the right of way.
• Pedestrians have priority at crosswalks. | Failure to yield can lead to traffic citations. | | **School‑Bus Rules** | • Drivers must stop when a school bus is loading or unloading children.
• No passing is allowed on either side of a stopped bus. | Violations can result in a $200 fine. | | **Lane‑Changing & Passing** | • Drivers must signal before changing lanes.
• Passing on the right is prohibited unless the left lane is occupied by a slower vehicle. | Improper lane changes can lead to citations. | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in front of fire hydrants, in crosswalks, or on sidewalks.
• Parking in a “no parking” zone can result in a $25 fine. | Some cities have additional local ordinances. | | **Traffic Signal Compliance** | • Red lights mean stop; green means go; yellow means prepare to stop.
• “Stop” signs require a full stop even if the intersection is clear. | Running a red light can lead to a $200 fine and points. | | **Points System** | • Texas uses a points system for traffic violations.
• Accumulating 12 points in 3 years can lead to license suspension. | Points vary by offense severity. | | **Insurance Requirements** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for total bodily injury, $25,000 for property damage. | Failure to maintain insurance can result in license suspension. | | **Special Vehicle Rules** | • Commercial vehicles must display a valid commercial driver’s license (CDL).
• Trucks over 10,000 lb must have a valid DOT inspection sticker. | Violations can lead to fines and vehicle impoundment. | ### Quick Reference - **Speed limit signs**: Look for posted signs; no‑limit highways have no posted limit. - **Seat belt**: All passengers must buckle up. - **Cell phone**: Use hands‑free only. - **DUI**: BAC ≥ 0.08% is illegal. - **School bus**: Stop and do not pass. - **Parking**: Follow posted signs; no parking in restricted zones. ### Where to Find More Information - **Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT)** – [https://www.txdot.gov](https://www.txdot.gov) - **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)** – [https://www.dps.texas.gov](https://www.dps.texas.gov) - **Texas Transportation Code** – Available online through the Texas Legislature website. Feel free to ask if you need details on a specific law or regulation!
